html:
In 1932 the Bahrain Petroleum Company struck oil at Jebel Dukhan in the middle of Bahrain. It was the first oil found on the Arab side of the Gulf.

The company was a subsidiary of Standard Oil of California, now Chevron. The find came just as the pearl trade collapsed, and oil money soon paid for schools, roads and a refinery at Sitra.

The geology of Bahrain persuaded the same company to look across the water in the Saudi mainland, where it found far more (Dammam No. 7, and Saudi Aramco). Bahrain's own fields were small, so it turned early to banking, aluminium and services.
sum: In 1932 the Bahrain Petroleum Company struck oil at Jebel Dukhan in the middle of Bahrain. It was the first oil found on the Arab side of the Gulf.
